rationale: The retained corpus and structured landscape satisfy the Research Contract. Coverage: 10 representative primary-source-analyzed papers span all 7 major KV Cache optimization routes identified in the 2025-2026 literature — eviction/token selection (LKV, CAKE, RocketKV), quantization (VQKV, QuantSpec), low-rank compression (KQ-SVD), sparse/dynamic top-k attention (NSA, RocketKV-HSA), architectural alternatives (NHA), prefix sharing/reuse systems (KVLink, LMCache), speculative decoding × cache (QuantSpec), and system scheduling/offloading (LMCache). Evidence quality: every PaperAnalysis with mechanism-level claims rests on inspect-source + read-source evidence (Methodology + Experiments sections), not abstracts. Recency: the corpus includes 2026 frontier work (NHA, RocketKV, QuantSpec, KVLink, LMCache) alongside 2025 foundational methods; frontier queries and native Web counter-search were performed per the latest/SOTA requirement. Contradictions handled: cross-route trade-offs (training-free vs training-aware, exact-retrieval vs compression) are captured in Findings and OpenProblems rather than flattened. Synthesis: 7 ApproachFamilies (real mechanism-based grouping), 8 Findings (cross-paper technical judgments with SUPPORTS sources + locators), 5 OpenProblems (field-level questions including very-long-context scalability, training-free quality, cross-route composition, multi-modal KV, and benchmark comparability). The newest retained paper dates, the searched recent window (2025-01 to 2026-08), frontier emerging-term queries, pagination, and native Web counter-search are all reflected in the retained state. No major route, representative method, or recent frontier development is missing that additional search would likely reveal.
